  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:07

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon (absent)
  Councilmember Steve Madison (absent)
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beat Bagneris
  Senior Assistant City Clerk Sandra Robles

  CEREMONIAL MATTERS Alex Hernandez, Assistant to the City Manager, announced that the
  City's Early Childhood Development and Early Learning Task Force
  received a $1.3 million grant from the Pasadena Community
  Foundation to assist those impacted by the Eaton Fire at local
  daycare centers. He also introduced Eva Rivera, the newly hired
  Program Coordinator III - Office of the Young Child.

  Ms. Rivera expressed her excitement for this opportunity to serve the
  youth of Pasadena, and to lend her support and expertise to this
  essential community. She also thanked members of the Early
  Learning Task Force, the Kidspace Children's Museum partnership,
  the Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) Board, PUSD
  Superintendent Dr. Elizabeth Blanco, Collaborate Pasadena, and
  Pasadena Child Health Foundation, for working collaboratively to
  support the youth in the community. She also announced details for
  the upcoming celebration for the Office of the Young Child to be held
  on Saturday, September 20, 2025 at Brookside Park.

  Mayor Gordo issued a proclamation declaring the month of October
  2025 as First Tee - Greater Pasadena Month, and expressed his
  gratitude to First Tee - Greater Pasadena for enhancing the lives of
  the youth through golf, promoting character development and core
  values. Matt Kohorst, 2nd Vice Chair of First Tee - Greater
  Pasadena, accepted the proclamation on behalf of the organization
  and thanked the City Council, the Rose Bowl Operating Company,
  and City staff, for their ongoing partnership and support.

  Council Minutes  2  09/15/2025
 PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Prior to public comment, Mayor Gordo reported that the issue
MATTERS NOT ON THE  regarding ethical investments has been referred to the Fire and
AGENDA  Police Retirement System Board due to the subject matter being
  under their jurisdiction. Councilmember Cole added that the FPRS
  Board will consider a request to potentially hold a special meeting to
  address the matter.

  The following individuals spoke on the humanitarian crisis in Gaza
  and/or advocated for the City to divest from specific companies.

  Mouna Stewart, Pasadena resident
  Brooklyn Kleckly, Pasadena resident
  Randall Heyn-Lamb, Pasadena resident
  Hedab Tariff, Pasadena resident
  Anaar Siletz, Pasadena resident
  Karin Fujii, Pasadena resident
  Edmond Mandin, Pasadena resident
  Michael Bannoura, Pasadena resident
  Brian Biery, Pasadena resident

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, requested that the City support Senate Bill
  274 regarding license plate reader regulations and advocated for the
  City to strengthen the Pasadena Police Department's license plate
  reader policy.

  Olden Denham, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City Council
  to agendize AB392 for continued discussion.

  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident, provided comments on the police
  officer involved shooting of Anthony McClain.

  Rene Gonzalez, Pasadena resident, provided comments
  recognizing Mexican Independence Day.

  Brian Weltman, Pasadena resident, requested assistance with sizing
  and modernizing residential solar.

  Jessica Kashiwabara, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns
  regarding federal immigration enforcement in local communities.

  Reverend Phillis Griffin, Pasadena Sister Cities, advocated for the
  City to establish a sister city relationship with the City of Guanajuato,
  Mexico.

  Councilmember Cole spoke on the war in Gaza and advocated for
  the City to support efforts to put an end to the war, regardless of the
  amount of power or influence the City may have in that regard.
